payload.summary: The repository is the official code for the paper "Tabular Deep Learning vs Classical ML for Urban Land Cover Classification" (NeurIPS 2025 MusIML workshop). It has one notebook, `Urban Land Cover Classification.ipynb`. The notebook has a "Random Forest" cell that trains a scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier and prints "Test Accuracy" with accuracy_score on the UCI test file. The test file is read as `urbantesting.csv`, which should be the UCI `testing.csv` renamed. The claim maps to this cell. The data files are not in the repo.

entrypoints.why: The only code file. Cells run in order: imports, load CSVs, validation split and LabelEncoder, z-score normalization, Logistic Regression, then Random Forest (the target cell, around source lines 282-320), then other classical models and PyTorch tabular DL models. The Random Forest cell uses RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=30, max_depth=5, min_samples_split=5, min_samples_leaf=3, max_features='log2', bootstrap=True, random_state=42). It fits on X_train_scaled and predicts on X_test_scaled.

dataFiles.why: Read with pd.read_csv in the notebook's 'Load Dataset' section. It is NOT in the repo. It must be the UCI Urban Land Cover training.csv, downloaded from https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/295/urban+land+cover and renamed. It must sit in the notebook's working directory, not in the `data/raw/` folder the README mentions.
Read with pd.read_csv. It is NOT in the repo. It must be the UCI testing.csv, renamed. It is the official test set that the accuracy is computed on.

metricSources.description: In the Random Forest cell, `test_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)` followed by `print(f"Test Accuracy: {test_accuracy:.4f}")`. y_test is the encoded 'class' column of urbantesting.csv. The same cell also prints macro precision, recall and F1, and AUC.

payload.runInstructions:
1. Download the UCI Urban Land Cover dataset (id 295). Copy training.csv to `urbantraining.csv` and testing.csv to `urbantesting.csv`, in the same directory as the notebook. The data cells use bare relative filenames.
2. Use Python 3.10+. Run `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Also install scipy (zscore is imported from it) and xlrd (imported at the top of the notebook), because neither is listed. Install torch only if running the DL cells. It isn't needed for the Random Forest cell.
3. Run the notebook cells in order through the Random Forest cell. Running the cells above it is required: imports, loading, split, scaling, and the Logistic Regression cell. The Logistic Regression cell defines `class_labels` and `y_test_binarized`, which the Random Forest cell uses for AUC. A non-interactive run such as `jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute` would also run the torch cells after it.
4. Read the 'Test Accuracy' line printed by the Random Forest cell.
warnings: The repository has no data files. The CSVs must come from UCI and be renamed from training.csv/testing.csv to urbantraining.csv/urbantesting.csv. I did not check the UCI files' column names. The notebook assumes a 'class' column.

requirements.txt is incomplete. The notebook imports scipy (zscore), xlrd, and torch (DL cells), and none of them is listed. The README's setup text also contradicts requirements.txt. Nothing pins versions.

The README paths do not match the repo. It refers to `notebooks/Urban Land Cover Classification.ipynb`, `data/raw/` and `outputs/metrics.csv`. The notebook is actually at the repo root, and the data is read from the working directory. I found no code that writes outputs/metrics.csv.

The validation split is `train_test_split(test_size=0.1, random_state=None)`. It is unseeded, so the 90% training subset changes on every run. Random Forest training data therefore varies between runs even though the model has random_state=42. Reproduced accuracy may differ slightly from the paper's.

The test features are z-scored with the test set's own mean and standard deviation (`X_test.apply(zscore)`), and the training and validation sets are each scaled separately. Scaling is not fit on the training data. This is a methodological quirk that affects the metric, but it is part of the official code.

The Random Forest hyperparameters are deliberately weak: depth 5, 30 trees, and comments saying 'less than 100'. They are not scikit-learn defaults. The paper's number should correspond to this configuration.
The notebook's saved outputs were removed from the checkout, so I could not read any reported value. The Random Forest cell is clearly the one that prints the test accuracy.

The Random Forest cell reuses `y_test_binarized` and `class_labels` from the Logistic Regression cell. Running it alone raises a NameError. Also, `LogisticRegression(multi_class='ovr')` is deprecated in newer scikit-learn. Newer versions may warn or fail, which would block the run before the Random Forest cell.

payload.summary: Run the reviewed project-owned adapter. It re-implements the notebook's Random Forest cells: 10% validation split with seed 42, per-split z-score as in the notebook, and RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=30, max_depth=5, min_samples_split=5, min_samples_leaf=3, max_features='log2', bootstrap=True, random_state=42). It fits on the training CSV and predicts on the official UCI testing.csv. It writes metrics.accuracyPercent to artifacts/result.json. The notebook can't run as a script and needs renamed CSV files, so the adapter is used. The dataset is the reviewed UCI zip, with training.csv and testing.csv extracted. The pinned requirements have binary wheels for linux/arm64 on Python 3.12. No compatibility constraints are needed.
